test_title: PYST 10: SSC CHSL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 03 Jul, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: 18 men can complete (1)/(5) of a work in 10 days. How many people are required to complete (2)/(5) of the same work in 5 days?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the MDH formula: (M₁ × D₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) / W₂

Given: (18 × 10) / (1/5) = (M₂ × 5) / (2/5)

⇒ 180 × 5 = M₂ × 5 × (5/2)

⇒ 180 = M₂ × (5/2)

⇒ M₂ = (180 × 2) / 5 = 72

**∴ The correct option is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial men (M₁) = 18

Initial days (D₁) = 10

Initial work (W₁) = 1/5

New days (D₂) = 5

New work (W₂) = 2/5

**Formula Used:**

(M₁ × D₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) / W₂

 CASE 1 Men (M1) = 18 Days (D1) = 10 Work (W1) = 1/5 CASE 2 Men (M2) = ? Days (D2) = 5 Work (W2) = 2/5 
• M1 × D1 / W1 = M2 × D2 / W2 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (18 × 10) / (1/5) = (M₂ × 5) / (2/5)

⇒ 180 × 5 = (M₂ × 5 × 5) / 2

⇒ 900 = (25 × M₂) / 2

⇒ 1800 = 25 × M₂

⇒ M₂ = 1800 / 25

⇒ M₂ = 72

**∴ The correct option is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Rule / Chain Rule

The general formula is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁ × E₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂ × E₂) / W₂, where M is men, D is days, H is hours, E is efficiency, and W is work.

Inverse Proportion

For a constant amount of work, the number of men is inversely proportional to the number of days taken: M₁D₁ = M₂D₂.

Work and Efficiency

Total work is the product of the number of workers, the time they work, and their individual efficiency: W = M × D × H × E.
